explanation: In Paradise Lost, published in 1667, Milton named the capital of Hell Pandaemonium, the place of all demons. The word later came to mean any wild uproar.

claims.text: John Milton coined the word Pandaemonium in Paradise Lost as the name of the capital of Hell.
Dante, Blake and Chaucer did not coin the word pandemonium.
Paradise Lost was first published in 1667.
Pandaemonium is built from Greek pan (all) and daimon (spirit, demon).
Pandemonium later came to mean a scene of wild uproar or chaos.
